name: Kepler's laws: conic geometry into planetary astronomy
summary: Planetary orbits became ellipses with area and period laws, replacing circle-based models.

name: Kepler: infinitesimal volumes of solids of revolution
summary: Volumes of revolved solids were found by summing infinitely many thin pieces.

name: Napier's logarithms
summary: Napier linked arithmetic and geometric progressions to speed trigonometric calculation; Briggs made decimal tables.

name: Fermat adequality
summary: An algebraic adequality rule found extrema and tangents of curves.

name: The calculus
summary: Tangent, quadrature and series techniques are unified into an algorithm with a notation, with the inverse relation between differentiation and integration as its core.

name: Indivisibles (Cavalieri)
summary: Cavalieri, Torricelli and Wallis computed areas by summing indivisible elements arithmetically.

name: Analytic geometry (Descartes, Fermat)
summary: Geometric problems were translated into algebraic equations, solved and classified by degree.

name: Fermat number theory
summary: Fermat's correspondence introduced the little theorem, four-square statement and other results.

name: Desargues projective geometry
summary: Properties invariant under projection, points at infinity and involution gave a unified theory of conics.

name: Saint-Vincent and Sarasa: area under hyperbola and logarithm
summary: Area under the hyperbola was shown to behave as a logarithm; Leibniz tied log to the integral of dy/y.
